evals.query: Java Kora 2 service, PostgreSQL, 3 replicas. Add a job that purges expired sessions every night at 02:00 and runs on only one replica.
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:scheduling-db-scheduler and io.koraframework:database-jdbc (versions from the io.koraframework:kora-bom 2.0.0.RC2 BOM), a PostgreSQL driver, and annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Extends JdbcDatabaseModule and DbSchedulerModule on the @KoraApp interface
Declares a @Root @Component that takes DbSchedulerWrapper in its constructor, explaining that DbSchedulerWrapper is not @Root and is otherwise pruned from the graph so no job runs
Uses @ScheduleWithCron("0 0 2 * * *") from io.koraframework.scheduling.db.scheduler.annotation on a no-argument method of a @Component, ideally with an explicit stable name
Creates the table via a Flyway/Liquibase migration named kora_scheduling_db_jobs (the default scheduling.dbScheduler.tableName), or sets tableName to scheduled_tasks when using the bundled SQL
Does not use the JDK or Quartz @ScheduleWithCron, does not add a ShedLock/Spring dependency, and does not invent a cluster flag

evals.query: I added DbSchedulerModule and a @ScheduleWithFixedDelay (db scheduler) job to my Kora 2 app. It compiles and starts, the table exists, but the job never runs and I see no 'SchedulingDbScheduler started' log. Why?
expected_behavior: Identifies that DbSchedulerWrapper is a @DefaultComponent that nothing depends on, and Kora resolves the graph only from @Root components, so the scheduler component is pruned
Fixes it with a @Root @Component whose constructor takes DbSchedulerWrapper (or com.github.kagkarlsson.scheduler.Scheduler)
Notes that the generated $<Class>_<method>_Job components are @Root, which is why the jobs exist but nothing runs them
Does not blame final/non-open classes or suggest reflection/Spring-style component scanning

evals.query: Show me the Kora 2 DB scheduler configuration: how many jobs run in parallel per instance, polling, table name, and shutdown.
expected_behavior: Uses the config path scheduling.dbScheduler (not scheduling.db or scheduling.dbscheduler)

Lists executionParallelism (default 10), tableName (default kora_scheduling_db_jobs), initializeTable (default false), shutdownWait (default 30s), polling.strategy (FETCH default, or LOCK_AND_FETCH), polling.prefetchMode (DEFAULT, BOUNDED, BUFFERED) and polling.interval (default 10s)
Explains executionParallelism is both db-scheduler's thread count and the limit of Kora's virtual-thread executor (threads named kora-db-scheduler-N)
Explains BOUNDED = 0.5/1.0 and BUFFERED = 0.75/2.0 lower/upper fraction-of-threads, DEFAULT keeps db-scheduler's own ratios
Mentions Configurer<SchedulerBuilder> for settings not exposed by the config
Does not invent keys such as scheduling.dbScheduler.enabled, threads or heartbeatInterval

evals.query: I added classpath:db/scheduling-db/flyway/postgresql to my Flyway locations for the Kora DB scheduler. Now Flyway complains about two migrations with version 1, and after renaming mine the scheduler logs SQL errors about kora_scheduling_db_jobs. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: Explains the bundled V1__create_scheduled_tasks.sql creates a table named scheduled_tasks while scheduling.dbScheduler.tableName defaults to kora_scheduling_db_jobs
Explains the bundled location carries its own V1__ which collides with the application's V1__ in the same Flyway history
Recommends copying the SQL into the application's own migration with the next free version and the table renamed to kora_scheduling_db_jobs, or alternatively setting tableName = "scheduled_tasks"
Notes db-scheduler logs startup-task errors and continues, so a restart is needed after fixing the table
Does not recommend initializeTable = true as the production answer

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2: I need a one-time job that runs 5 minutes after deploy on only one of my pods. Can I use @ScheduleOnce from the DB scheduler, and what happens on the next deploy or if it fails?
expected_behavior: Uses @ScheduleOnce(delay = 5, unit = ChronoUnit.MINUTES, name = "...") from io.koraframework.scheduling.db.scheduler.annotation on a no-argument, non-suspend member function of a @Component class, with ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors")
Explains it is scheduled on startup only if no execution is pending, so concurrent pod starts create one execution and one pod runs it
States that after it runs the row is removed, so a later restart or deploy schedules it again — it is once per startup wave, not once ever
States that a failure removes the execution without retry
Includes the @Root DbSchedulerStarter-style component depending on DbSchedulerWrapper

evals.query: After I renamed my Kora DB-scheduled job class from CleanupJob to SessionCleanupJob, the job ran immediately on deploy and there is an old row left in the scheduler table. Also a colleague's module now fails with 'Duplicate key CleanupJob#run'. Explain.
expected_behavior: Explains the default task name is SimpleClassName#method and it is the job's persistent identity in the table
Explains the rename created a new task (new row, initialDelay/first cron time applied again) and left the old row as an unresolved execution that db-scheduler logs and eventually deletes
Explains Duplicate key comes from two jobs resolving to the same task name, e.g. same simple class name and method in different packages
Recommends an explicit stable name on the annotation or in config
Does not suggest deleting the whole table as the fix

evals.query: How does a long-running Kora DB-scheduler job behave on SIGTERM? Could it lose its database connection mid-run?
expected_behavior: Explains DbSchedulerWrapper.release() calls db-scheduler Scheduler.stop(): polling stops, running executions get scheduling.dbScheduler.shutdownWait, then their virtual threads are interrupted and it waits up to another shutdownWait
Explains the wrapper depends on the jobs and the DataSource, so it is released before them and a draining job keeps its connection pool
Recommends bounding the job body and honouring interruption, and making work idempotent because an interrupted or dead execution may run again
Does not claim the job is never interrupted and does not reference scheduling.jdk.shutdownWait for this module

evals.query: We run 5 replicas of a Kora 2 service. I put @ScheduleWithFixedDelay(delay = 10, unit = ChronoUnit.MINUTES) from io.koraframework.scheduling.jdk.annotation on our invoice-sending job and customers got 5 copies. Fix it.
expected_behavior: Explains that the JDK scheduler is in-process and stateless, so every replica runs every job

Moves the job to scheduling-db-scheduler: DbSchedulerModule, @ScheduleWithFixedDelay from io.koraframework.scheduling.db.scheduler.annotation with a stable name, the scheduler table, and a @Root component depending on DbSchedulerWrapper
Notes the DB module has no fixed-rate annotation, so fixed delay or cron is used
Recommends making the invoice sending idempotent, since dead executions are revived on another replica
Does not propose a hand-written database lock or leader election around the JDK job, and does not keep the JDK annotation

evals.query: Kora 2 DB scheduler: I copied @ScheduleWithCron("0 0 3 1 JAN ? 2027") from our Quartz job onto a method, importing ScheduleWithCron from io.koraframework.scheduling.db.scheduler.annotation, and the app fails at startup. Why, and what should I use?
expected_behavior: Explains the DB scheduler passes the expression to db-scheduler's CronSchedule, which uses Spring-style six-field cron (seconds first, no year field) and fails graph init on an invalid pattern
States that the 7-field expression with a year field is valid for Quartz and for Kora's JDK CronExpression but not for the DB scheduler
Rewrites the expression in six-field Spring form, or routes to kora-aop-scheduling-quartz when exact Quartz cron semantics are required
Mentions that the value "-" disables a DB cron job
Does not claim the DB module uses Kora's JDK CronExpression or Quartz CronExpression
